convoLines.text: "Yeah — What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
"Still on what scares you most. Seen worse."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
Elmarie: "Hey — come here. You should hear this."
"Bulldozer — Lowers its head, paws the earth. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
"a ridge with a view for miles — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"Still on the kindest thing someone's done for you."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"That's enough for now. It'll percolate."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You said the scary part is this might be on purpose. That someone's watching. Believing it more or less these days?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Chickweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Carolina is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Sleep's gone strange. I check the treeline every hour at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Worrying about its motives doesn't fill the pantry. Focus on what's in front of you."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me about people sharing food they couldn't spare. Quiet. No performance. Seen it again since?"
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
You walk to the trap line with Elmarie. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Bottom line: Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Greenbrier Shoots — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.

"We never finished talking about that personal stuff — we wandered off it, 7 days back. 'You show them Chickweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Huh. They turn it over in their mind. I'll…' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Like I said — Still on that personal stuff."
They let that thread drop — for now.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "You want to know what I did in the raid? I put down Hushpuppy at the treeline. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"My part? I was at the door. I'll be at the door again."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Honest. I can work with honest."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on your plan here. Just... be straight with me."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
On the way, Sanjay stops and actually teaches you something — how they read a slope for water, how their grandmother did it. (Knowledge, freely given. The Codex notes it.)
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Give it time."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"I wasn't a midwife. I was a Firefighter. I keep my head down. Old habit. It kept me alive before; it keeps me alive now."
"That again?" Sanjay sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I tried the Chickweed like you showed me. Didn't poison anyone, so that's a win."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Greta. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"My wound needs a second pair of hands. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said one day at a time. How's that holding — still day by day, or are you thinking further out yet?"
"Take your time."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Have you seen the sick row? 2 down with a hot angry fever. Nobody says it out loud but everyone's counting."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
You show them Greenbrier Shoots — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I've got things to see to. Don't be a stranger."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"This was good." They mean it.

"Autumn and I never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 14 days back. You weren't there for that one — Autumn was. Want to hear where it left off? 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
They nod. "Okay."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Names are for when it's dead or known. Right now it's neither, so I taste the water before the others drink instead."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them American Hazelnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Halfway to the ridge, Hendrik freezes. Fresh tracks — big. "We go back now. Quietly." You do. The wild, reminding you.
"Right, so — You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Still on that question. Just... be straight with me."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Have you heard what they're calling Buffering? Sanjay is pushing 'Loud-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. I wanted to ask rather than assume."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

recoverHome: d7: That night, they bring Carolina home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d7: SYSTEM: Neural interface stable. Text overlay enabled.
d7: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 22. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 2."

d7: ◈ THE SPARK — something clicks. A trick Autumn learned long ago suddenly has edges it never had. SYSTEM: "ANOMALY: organic unit demonstrates pattern recognition. Slot capacity increased. We are taking notes." (Ability slots: 2)
d7: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
d7: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
d7: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d7: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
d8: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d8: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."

d8: ◈ SYSTEM: "RATINGS DIP. The audience wants STAKES — pointed ones. A PALISADE. Stockpile 14,000 kcal, 350 wood and 60 stone. Walls make such good television. You will thank us when the teeth come."
